clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman with a complex medical history including stroke, right internal carotid artery occlusion, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, chronic kidney disease, and chronic hepatitis B presented to nephrology with intermittent lower abdominal cramping. She had been evaluated 2 years prior for proteinuria with kidney biopsy. At the current presentation, laboratory studies showed advanced CKD (serum creatinine 2.86 mg/dL, eGFR 17.18 mL/min/1.73 m²) with heavy proteinuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio 2790.6 mg/g creatinine). Echocardiography confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with elevated left ventricular mass index (163.5 g/m²). Initial screening tests for Fabry disease showed normal α-galactosidase enzyme activity (3.02 µmol/h/L) and normal plasma lyso-Gb3 (< 1.00 ng/mL). However, kidney biopsy electron microscopy revealed lamellated lipid inclusions in podocytes, pathognomonic for Fabry disease. Genetic testing identified GLA gene variants (CIH variants: c.−10 C > T, c.369 + 990 C > A, c.370–81_370–77delCAGCC, c.640–16 A > G, c.1000–22 C > T). The patient was initiated on enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with agalsidase-β 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Within the early period of ERT, abdominal pain was substantially reduced. During 2 years of follow-up with ERT, eGFR declined to 9.87 mL/min/1.73 m², while echocardiography showed no progression of left ventricular hypertrophy with slightly decreased left ventricular mass index (152.8 g/m²), indicating stabilization of cardiac involvement.

final.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman with a complex medical history including stroke, right internal carotid artery occlusion, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, chronic kidney disease, and chronic hepatitis B presented to nephrology with intermittent lower abdominal cramping. She had been evaluated 2 years prior for proteinuria with kidney biopsy. At the current presentation, laboratory studies showed advanced CKD (serum creatinine 2.86 mg/dL, eGFR 17.18 mL/min/1.73 m²) with heavy proteinuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio 2790.6 mg/g creatinine). Echocardiography confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with elevated left ventricular mass index (163.5 g/m²). Initial screening tests for Fabry disease showed normal α-galactosidase enzyme activity (3.02 µmol/h/L) and normal plasma lyso-Gb3 (< 1.00 ng/mL). However, kidney biopsy electron microscopy revealed lamellated lipid inclusions in podocytes, pathognomonic for Fabry disease. Genetic testing identified GLA gene variants (CIH variants: c.−10 C > T, c.369 + 990 C > A, c.370–81_370–77delCAGCC, c.640–16 A > G, c.1000–22 C > T). The patient was initiated on enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with agalsidase-β 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Within the early period of ERT, abdominal pain was substantially reduced. During 2 years of follow-up with ERT, eGFR declined to 9.87 mL/min/1.73 m², while echocardiography showed no progression of left ventricular hypertrophy with slightly decreased left ventricular mass index (152.8 g/m²), indicating stabilization of cardiac involvement.
